Metabolite Quality Control

quality_control.Rmd

Introduction

Metabolomics data often contain missing values, outliers, and features that require filtering before downstream analysis. The metabolite_qc() function provides an efficient and automated way to perform quality control (QC) on a Metabolites object.

This vignette walks through the key parameters and steps for performing QC using this function.

Creating a Metabolites Object

Before performing QC, you need a Metabolites object, which contains metabolomics data along with metadata.

library(metaboprep2)

# Example Metabolon (format 1) raw data file
filepath <- system.file("extdata", "metabolon_v1_example.xlsx", package = "metaboprep2")

# Create a Metabolites object with the desired parameters
metabolites <- Metabolites(project_name              = "ExampleProject", 
                           filepath                  = filepath,
                           format                    = "metabolon_v1",   
                           feature_missingness       = 0.2,
                           sample_missingness        = 0.2,
                           total_peak_area_sd        = 5,
                           outlier_udist             = 5,
                           outlier_treatment         = "leave_be",
                           winsorize_quantile        = 1,
                           tree_cut_height           = 0.5,
                           pc_outlier_sd             = 5,
                           derived_var_exclusion     = TRUE,
                           xenobiotics_var_exclusion = TRUE)

# Import the data 
metabolites <- import_data(metabolites)

Performing Metabolite Quality Control

The metabolite_qc() function applies multiple QC filters based on missingness, outlier detection, PCA-based QC. This generates another layer to the data matrices named post_qc.

metabolites <- metabolite_qc(metabolites, source = "raw")
#> 
#> ── Starting Metabolite QC Process ──────────────────────────────────────────────
#> ℹ Validating input parameters...

#> ℹ Analysing exclusions...
#> ℹ Applying exclusion of derived features...
#> ✔ Derived features exclusions assessment complete. (0 features excluded)
#> ℹ Applying exclusion of xenobiotic features...
#> ✔ Xenobiotic features exclusions assessment complete. (3 features excluded)
#> ℹ Assessing for extreme sample missingness >=80%...
#> ✔ Extreme sample missingness exclusions assessment complete. (0 samples excluded)
#> ℹ Assessing for extreme feature missingness >=80%...

Accessing QC’d data

There are two primary ways to access data stored in a Metabolites object:

  1. Using the @ operator to directly access object slots.
  2. Using getter functions like get_data() for structured data extraction.

Accessing Data Using @ Operator 

metabolites@data[, , "post_qc"][1:5,1:5]
#>      compid_123 compid_124 compid_125 compid_126 compid_127
#> ind1         NA         NA         NA         NA         NA
#> ind2  1.2057866   1.428384  1.2262280  0.7742638  1.1269745
#> ind3         NA   1.495705         NA  1.0636195  0.8006724
#> ind4  0.6731959   1.128572  1.2227678  0.7767174  1.0132617
#> ind5  0.8260065   1.291734  0.8725828  1.2589163  0.8209024

Accessing Data Using Getter Functions 

get_data(metabolites, layer="post_qc", drop=TRUE)[1:5,1:5]
#>      compid_123 compid_124 compid_125 compid_126 compid_127
#> ind2  1.2057866   1.428384  1.2262280  0.7742638  1.1269745
#> ind3         NA   1.495705         NA  1.0636195  0.8006724
#> ind4  0.6731959   1.128572  1.2227678  0.7767174  1.0132617
#> ind5  0.8260065   1.291734  0.8725828  1.2589163  0.8209024
#> ind6  1.0033843   1.027972  1.1651089  1.0049920  0.6529416

Accessing Only Data Passing QC 

get_data(metabolites, layer="post_qc", drop=TRUE)[1:5,1:5]
#>      compid_123 compid_124 compid_125 compid_126 compid_127
#> ind2  1.2057866   1.428384  1.2262280  0.7742638  1.1269745
#> ind3         NA   1.495705         NA  1.0636195  0.8006724
#> ind4  0.6731959   1.128572  1.2227678  0.7767174  1.0132617
#> ind5  0.8260065   1.291734  0.8725828  1.2589163  0.8209024
#> ind6  1.0033843   1.027972  1.1651089  1.0049920  0.6529416

Exclusions

The underlying data still has all respresentations of the samples and features, however, the QC process builds a matrix of exclusion reasons.

Accessing the Exclusions List 

str(metabolites@exclusions)
#> List of 3
#>  $ raw    :List of 2
#>   ..$ samples :List of 4
#>   .. ..$ extreme_sample_missingness       : chr(0) 
#>   .. ..$ user_defined_sample_missingness  : chr(0) 
#>   .. ..$ user_defined_sample_totalpeakarea: chr(0) 
#>   .. ..$ user_defined_sample_pca_outlier  : chr(0) 
#>   ..$ features:List of 2
#>   .. ..$ extreme_feature_missingness     : chr(0) 
#>   .. ..$ user_defined_feature_missingness: chr(0) 
#>  $ qcing  :List of 2
#>   ..$ samples :List of 4
#>   .. ..$ extreme_sample_missingness       : chr(0) 
#>   .. ..$ user_defined_sample_missingness  : chr [1:2] "ind9" "ind59"
#>   .. ..$ user_defined_sample_totalpeakarea: chr(0) 
#>   .. ..$ user_defined_sample_pca_outlier  : chr "ind1"
#>   ..$ features:List of 2
#>   .. ..$ extreme_feature_missingness     : chr(0) 
#>   .. ..$ user_defined_feature_missingness: chr(0) 
#>  $ post_qc:List of 2
#>   ..$ samples :List of 4
